newsitem.title: USA: Glickman says deplores politicization of biotech.
newsitem.headline: Glickman says deplores politicization of biotech.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman lamented Thursday the politicization of biotech food products and said the United States would persevere in making "good science" the deciding factor in the food debate.

"Clearly, we see it in the rest of the world, where this issue has become a highly charged, political issue," Glickman told attendees at a consulting-firm conference. "It's going to take a lot of perseverance...to try to get the truth out.
"And the truth is, good science is the dominant issue here in making these decisions."
Two new U.S. biotech products have drawn fire in Europe. One is a soybean that was genetically engineered for tolerance to a pesticide. The other is a corn altered to produce a biopesticide.
The soybean has been approved for sale in the European Union. Officials have yet to rule on the corn.
"We think we're having success in terms of the soybeans, for instance, in Europe," Glickman said.
"We'll continue to do our best to insure, in fact, that good science dominates the discussion of those issues."

U.S. officials say both products are safe. Foes want consumers to refuse to use the products and to demand labeling of foods containing them, steps that the grain industry says would be unduly expensive and unnecessary.
